objection.quote: Inductively, after the first $j+1$ columns have been swept, either one whole $d$-strip remains uncancelled in the odd row, or a cut has occurred in every one of these $j+1$ columns: adding the next column, whose $2^{j+1}$ strips consist of two identical copies of all preceding strips plus one parity interchange, preserves this alternative.
objection.witness: NON-SEQUITUR (with a false sub-claim). Premises established: heights are $d,2d,\dots,2^q d$ cut into $d$-strips, and $\Delta=\int (N(t)\bmod 2)dt$. The structural claim is arithmetically false for $j\ge 1$: columns $d,2d,\dots,2^j d$ contain $(2^{j+1}-1)$ strips of height $d$, so 'two identical copies of all preceding strips plus one' would be $2^{j+2}-1$ strips, whereas the next column has only $2^{j+1}$ strips (equality only when $j=0$). Moreover Xiang's splits may be at arbitrary heights, not at multiples of $d$, so the dichotomy 'a whole $d$-strip remains uncancelled, or a cut occurred in every column' is never derived for arbitrary cut positions; no argument is given for why adding a column preserves the alternative under a cut placed at a non-strip level. Hence the conclusion 'with at most $s$ cuts an odd strip remains' does not follow.
objection.load_bearing: Section 3 derives Liu's guarantee solely from Lemma (ii) applied with $q=n$, $d=1/D$; this induction step is the entire proof of Lemma (ii), so the lower bound stands or falls with it.
